claim.quote: yielding m_W = 80370 +/- 7 (stat.) +/- 11 (exp. syst.) +/- 14 (mod. syst.) MeV = 80370 +/- 19 MeV

date.note: arXiv submission date; published as Eur. Phys. J. C 78, 110 (2018).

name: Measurement of the W boson mass

significance.note: A measurement, not a discovery; no significance is quoted.

summary.plain: ATLAS measured the mass of the W boson, a carrier of the weak force, from 7 TeV collision data recorded in 2011 (7.8 million W→μν and 5.9 million W→eν candidates), obtaining 80370 ± 19 MeV.
summary.technical: W → lepton ν candidates from 4.6 fb⁻¹ of 7 TeV data, template fits to lepton transverse momentum and transverse mass: m_W = 80370 ± 19 MeV, combining statistical, experimental-systematic and modelling uncertainties.

title: Measurement of the W-boson mass in pp collisions at sqrt(s)=7 TeV with the ATLAS detector
why_it_matters: In the Standard Model the W-boson mass is related to the top-quark and Higgs-boson masses through a radiative correction that is sensitive to them, and in extended theories that correction receives contributions from additional particles. The paper says that improving the precision of the W-mass measurement is of high importance for testing the overall consistency of the Standard Model.
